note: The electrolyte model (GAME_SPEC §10): Pitzer's equations at 25 C, used at every temperature. a_phi and b: the Debye-Huckel term. pairs: a cation and an anion, named as in species.json's ions, with beta0, beta1, beta2, c_phi and the exponents alpha1, alpha2. A pair not listed has no specific interaction. diffusion: each ion's diffusion coefficient at 25 C, scaled to other temperatures as T / viscosity (GAME_SPEC §7); an ion not listed puts no limit on transport. viscosity: the solvent's (water's, at 0.5 MPa: the liquid to 150 C), mPa s, by rising temperature; read between points in its logarithm, held beyond the ends. solvent: saturated liquid water's properties by temperature (Lienhard, A Heat Transfer Textbook 6.00, Table A.3: rho kg/m3, cp J/kg K, k W/m K, alpha and nu m2/s, Pr, beta 1/K), read between rows, held beyond the ends: its density, for what floats on what (a column's layers, GAME_SPEC §6), its conduction, and boiling's bubbles (§11). water_ionisation: water's own ionisation, whose constant Kw sets the pH where neither an acid nor a base is left over. Sources: docs/DATA_SOURCES.md.

diffusion.note: each ion's diffusion coefficient in water at infinite dilution, 25 C, m2/s (GAME_SPEC §7)
diffusion.source_87: (Stage 87) I-: the CRC Handbook, Vanysek, Ionic conductivity and diffusion at infinite dilution (76.8 S cm2/mol, 2.045e-9 m2/s); H2O2: van Stroe-Biezen, Everaerts, Janssen and Tacken 1993 (Anal. Chim. Acta 273, 553), Table 2, in 0.1 M phosphate buffer at 25 C
diffusion.source_76: (Stage 76) Ca2+, Mg2+, Ba2+, Fe2+, Al3+, NO3- and Zn2+: PHREEQC v3 phreeqc.dat -dw; Ag+, Fe3+ and Co2+: the CRC Handbook (Vanysek), as aqion.de's table gives it; FeOH2+ and AlOH2+ their aquo ions' (no measurement read)
diffusion.source_64: (Stage 64) the new ions: the CRC Handbook, Vanysek, Ionic conductivity and diffusion at infinite dilution; dissolved CO2 and NH3: PHREEQC v3 phreeqc.dat -dw; acetic acid, phosphoric acid and the indicators: the Wilke-Chang and Hayduk-Minhas correlations, their mean (no measurement read)
diffusion.source_82: (Stage 82) Li+ and Sr2+: the CRC Handbook (Vanysek), 1.029e-9 and 0.791e-9 (PHREEQC's -dw 1.03e-9 and 0.794e-9 within 0.4 %)

walden.note: (Stage 65) each ion's mobility with temperature, Walden's rule with an exponent of its own: D goes as T / viscosity^p from 25 C, lambda0 viscosity^p held; default: every ion's (a neutral solute keeps Stokes and Einstein's 1); H+'s own, its protons hopping (Grotthuss)
walden.source: calibrated: default to the KCl standards at 0 and 18 C (Jones and Bradshaw 1933, as MacInnes 1939 Table 3-I gives them), H+ to HCl's limiting equivalent conductance from 0 to 45 C (Hamer and DeWane, NSRDS-NBS 33, 1970, Table 12), each on this table's viscosity

gas_viscosity.note: (Stage 79) a gas's viscosity, air's at 1 atm (GAME_SPEC §6, Pistons: a tube's flow of gas, Poiseuille's compressible form), by temperature, read between rows, held beyond the ends
gas_viscosity.source: Engineering ToolBox, Air - Dynamic and Kinematic Viscosity, at 1 atm (μPa s): within 1 % of Lemmon and Jacobsen's (Int. J. Thermophys. 25, 21, 2004)

conductivity.note: (Stage 65) a solution's conductivity (GAME_SPEC §10): each ion's limiting molar conductivity by Nernst and Einstein from its diffusion, lowered by Debye, Huckel and Onsager's relaxation and electrophoresis over 1 + B a sqrt(I) (Robinson and Stokes); dielectric: water's dielectric constant by temperature, read between rows, held beyond the ends; ion_size_angstrom: a, one for every ion
conductivity.source: dielectric: Malmberg and Maryott 1956, as Hamer and DeWane (NSRDS-NBS 33, 1970) Table 2 gives it; ion_size_angstrom: calibrated to KCl's and NaCl's (Shedlovsky 1932, as MacInnes 1939 Table 18-II gives them) and HCl's (NSRDS-NBS 33 Table 11) at 0.1 mol/L, 25 C

density.note: the solvent's density at 1 atm (Stage 67: what a liquid's and a solute's volume grow by with temperature), kg/m^3: (a0 + a1 t + ... + a5 t^5) / (1 + b t), t in C, its range in C; beyond it, its value and slope at the end

compressibility.note: the solvent's isothermal compressibility at 1 atm (Stage 88: what a sealed cell's liquids give to its pressure, GAME_SPEC §6), 1/kPa as the source prints it: (a0 + a1 t + ... + a5 t^5) / (1 + b t), t in C, its range in C; beyond it, its value and slope at the end
